reviews.text: Just an all around basic tower defense game with a few minor unique quirks here and there. I can definitely see myself putting in at least 10 hours into this although the game does have its flaws. Overall I think it just needs more content and extra polish. There's so many areas i could mention for improvement but too many for me to be bothered noting down. I recommend the devs simply spend more time playing, tweaking the game and continuing to listen to player feedback. Off the top of my head, i recall the interfaces for towers often obstructing my view. In general it's too hard and inconvenient to deselect something. From a gameplay standard, I don't like how you essentially have to brute force your way through waves. You need to lose to research better upgrades so there's a certain point in every run that you won't be able to get through a wave with skill alone, unless i'm missing something. Ultimately where the game stands at launch, there doesn't seem to be anything special about it to set it apart from other games in the genre let alone in general and without that extra something, i think i wouldn't want to pay more than 7 dollars at absolute most for this. In other words, good game, good potential. 20 bucks is too much for where it stands now

Game is really grindy. If you passed wave 26 you are doing well. But let's explain game more: - Game is based on cards/loot boxes chance. - There is a tech tree and you get research point per each wave in game. - Maps are randomly generated and you unlock new piece of land every turn/wave. The monsters attack when you select new tile to discover. - You gain minerals (cash) per each monster you kill and you can also mine the resources (don't bother) - You have two basic towers at your disposal from the beginning: Gatling tower and cannon tower. - You can research more towers but this is locked behind chance/luck per each game. Works basically like loot boxes, you never know what you will get. - You can get common/rare/epic/legendary items + tower unlocks + research point and minerals/cash. Most of the time (80%-90%) you get common lol. - There are some strategy aspects in the game like: terrain height (you gain range on towers) and you can also set towers to target different monsters. - Monsters have life/armor/shield that different tower can target. There are also Bosses in the game. Well I have spend 10h in this game grinding and trying to find best way to play it. The further I have reached is wave 31. After wave 25+ monsters are super fast and have all kind of health. I guess you have to grind this game over 40h to beat it further. But honestly what is the point. After 10h I feel like I have just wasted my time playing the game. The biggest problem this game has is that everything is based on chance/luck and it is definitely not on your side! No matter what you do you will loose around wave 26. Pros: - cheap game - runs great on 4k - graphics are good Cons: - loot boxes - Better towers unlocked by loot boxes - Lots of grinding - Gets very repetitive - Don't give satisfaction - you play and you don't progress I will keep playing from time to time but as this game is early access there is still lots to fix and balance.

Incredibly grindy. RNG based with gambling/casino elements in the for of loot boxes. Enemies past wave 20 seem to be able to run through your towers without a care in the world even if you build tazer and acid turrets. It starts out fun but after a few hours it becomes frustrating and annoying watching the enemy run through your turret layout. Might come back in a few months and check out to see if the balance has been sorted. But if you're looking to get punished, give it a go.

It's not a bad tower defense game per se. It just doesn't offer anything new. It's your usual Tower Game where you expand as you go with a massive tech-tree to unlock incremental improvements. No interesting mechanics beyond that. The art style is pretty basic, and any scenario or story non-existent. It's just a very basic, looks-and-mechanics-wise, TD. Buy it if it drops to less than $5 and you have nothing better to do.

I am an Avid TD fan with over 100+ of them in my steam library alone. Mineral Defense is a really good TD game with one of the biggest research/upgrade sections I've seen, I think the only thing in there that you cant upgrade is penis size, although I suppose that comes about just playing the game. Every time you run a new level the path is always different and can be maxed out at 25x25 grids, tower variety is great and with mineral deposits also randomly generated it can be a nightmare, like when you find a massive gold deposit... and your cant mine it XD. The power creep of each wave seems bang on and having to have a wide variety of towers to remove armour/shields/HP is a great touch as in most TD's you can get away with spamming the same 2-3 towers each level, this games mechanics require you to build alternate towers as the waves progress. The Developers/Publishers have been incredible too, they are active in there discord and we also contacted them for a live twitch stream promotion and they sources us extra keys to give away to the community which I am extremely grateful for. (we may have 1 or 2 keys left over if anyone wants to try it out) Currently there are only 2 planets to run on Lava & Frozen, would be nice if they added in a couple more into the game like a forest/desert/sea based ones and doubled up on the achievements too which would add double the amount of play time to the game.

Bullet sponge simulator and a very frustrating game. Everything is just random which means you will only win if RNGesus loves you no matter what meta progression upgrades you have. The meta progression just barely makes the game somehow functional, that is if you grind for all of them. Speaking of RNGesus, its always very frustrating to start a round just to get some path splittings right after your start point... and of course mostly another next to it as well with no area to kill the enemies. The balance... does not exist. Sometimes you can beat some waves with ease just to get crushed at the next one without any reason at all. Most Bosses walk through your maze as if it was nothing while all your towers blast at them. Some enemies are so fast, that even multiple points with 6 or more maxed out Slow-Towers in a row wont stop them. The UI Update is horrible. It went from a clean and easy to understand interface to a colorful kids playground with bright colors, horrible controls and missing info and a clusterf*ck of tower menu. Before the update everything was nice, readable and functional, now its eye cancer. Achievements are made for masochists willing to spend hundreds of hours to kill 50k Yetis which btw only spawns in at later waves. So even if you made it this far, you kill about a few of them, maybe up to a hundred... do the math yourself of how many games you have to play. Don't forget to add the amount of failed attempts to even get to the Yeti spawns. Game started okay, then the Updates came and made it worse.

Its a complicated recommendation. But i very much enjoy playing this. Pros; -very well balanced towers -roguelite elements via research add alot of longevity and complexity in builds, in some ways superior to my other favourite TD, Nordhold (100% recommend that game) -smooth as butter performance -difficulty scaling and resource demands scale extremely well -exploring the research trees is alot of fun and i don't feel punished for lateral upgrading alot Cons; -dull aesthetic, only 2 maps, 1 of which is locked out until you've spent at least ~5+ hours playing. -artstyle is mid -relatively few, and restrictive options in the graphics tab (as in, i can have vsync enabled, or i can pick my fps, i can't do both, and fps options don't match up with my monitor, 120-240fps is a rather confusing jump) -music sucks (not a really big problem however, i just put on a music stream playlist instead, i do this for loads of games these days) -no VA work at all, and mediocre sound effects outside of that, generally the audio is poor all around, i'd like the turrets to have a more punchy sound, but to be fair it'd be hard to balance the audio when you have 50+ different turrets blazing away simultaneously -i have to restart the game like 5-10x at the very start of each session, to get the lucky roll where loads of mineral resources spawn around my base, which is tedious, albeit the restarts are very quick and don't strain my pc at all, but frankly it should just be adjusted for lots of mineral spawns every time, its a 5x differential between normal spawns and high-resource spawns, pointless. -no custom in-game mouse option, during heavy play it can be extremely hard to see your own little white cursor, its one of the very few games to NOT have a custom in-game cursor as default, a strange and baffling omission from game design. Overall, very compelling game, but the dev needs to hire an art director/vfx artist to spice the game up, sacrifice a little performance for alot better aesthetics, it'll definitely improve sales. Otherwise the games loads of fun and very addictive.
